outcome: No proof of the invariants conjecture (lambda = mu = 0 for totally real fields, all primes p) or of the generalized pseudo-null conjecture appears in any source I could read. Since 26 January 2024 the number-field results are family-restricted verifications, conditional reductions and a finite numerical check. The one 2026 claim that the invariants conjecture is resolved (Wikipedia's lead, citing arXiv 2609.40282, submitted 30 September 2026) rests on a paper about elliptic curves over Q at Eisenstein primes, which does not address totally real number fields.
problem_asks: Written from the bullet name 'Greenberg's conjectures' and from the current Wikipedia article's description of them (retrieved 11 October 2026); the frozen January 2024 wording was not retrieved. (a) The invariants conjecture (Greenberg's 1971 thesis; reformulated 1976): for a totally real number field k and any prime p, the Iwasawa invariants lambda_p(k) and mu_p(k) of the cyclotomic Z_p-extension of k are both zero; equivalently the p-parts of the class groups A_n of the layers k_n stay uniformly bounded as n grows. (b) The generalized conjecture (Greenberg 2001; 'pseudo-null'): for a totally real field F, the Galois group X~ of the pro-p Hilbert class field of the Z_p-tower over F is a pseudo-null module over the Iwasawa algebra; the article also gives an equivalent form for a general number field k and prime p. (c) Stated in the same article as a further related unsolved conjecture: mu_l(k) = 0 for every number field k and every prime l (proved by Ferrero and Washington only for abelian extensions of Q). (d) The rationality conjecture (Greenberg, 2016, per the article): for every odd prime p and every integer t >= 1 there is a p-rational number field K, Galois over Q, with Gal(K/Q) isomorphic to (Z/2Z)^t. Adjacent, not in the article body: the elliptic-curve conjecture named after Greenberg (1990s): for E/Q with good ordinary reduction at p and E[p] irreducible, the algebraic mu-invariant of the p-Selmer group of E over the cyclotomic Z_p-extension of Q vanishes. The article cites a paper on that elliptic-curve case in support of its 2026 claim, so it is recorded below. Whether (c), (d) and the elliptic-curve version were inside the January 2024 bullet is not established by anything I retrieved.

events.what_happened: Adithya Chakravarthy, arXiv:2405.05871 (single version, 9 May 2024), 'The Iwasawa mu-invariant of certain elliptic curves of analytic rank zero': new cases of Greenberg's elliptic-curve mu = 0 conjecture for some elliptic curves E/Q of analytic rank 0, via the p-adic L-function and a Rankin-Selberg method.
events.delivers: Mu = 0 for the p-Selmer group over Q^cyc of certain elliptic curves E/Q with good ordinary reduction at p, E[p] irreducible and analytic rank 0 (the exact conditions were not read; the abstract says 'some elliptic curves'). Elliptic-curve namesake only; no statement about lambda or mu of totally real number fields.
events.remains: The elliptic-curve conjecture for all curves of that type, and the number-field invariants conjecture entirely.
events.direction: Consistent with the elliptic-curve mu = 0 conjecture, which it proves for some curves; no counterexample. Not about the bullet's number-field statement.

events.what_happened: Adithya Chakravarthy, arXiv:2408.07826, 'The Iwasawa mu-invariants of Elliptic Curves over Q'. v1 (14 Aug 2024) claimed mu = 0 for almost all good ordinary primes p of an elliptic curve E/Q. v2 (28 Oct 2024) says the v1 argument had a mistake, which two named readers pointed out, and now claims only mu <= 1 for all but finitely many good ordinary primes.
events.revisions: v1 14 Aug 2024 (claimed mu = 0 for almost all good ordinary p); v2 28 Oct 2024 (weakened to mu <= 1 for all but finitely many p).
events.delivers: For an elliptic curve E/Q: mu <= 1 for all but finitely many good ordinary primes p. This is a bound, not mu = 0 for any prime. Elliptic-curve namesake only.
events.remains: mu = 0 for elliptic curves over Q (the conjecture itself), and the number-field invariants conjecture entirely.

checked_by.who: Lei and R. Gajek-Leonard (names as given on the arXiv v2 comment; Lei's first name not recorded)
checked_by.qualification: Iwasawa theorists; Gajek-Leonard later posted arXiv:2409.18021 on a similar bound in the supersingular setting
checked_by.what_they_did: Identified the mistake in v1, per the author's v2 note ('which Lei and Gajek-Leonard pointed out')

events.time_since_posted: about 26 months for v1; about 23 months for v2
events.doubts: The v1 claim was wrong, as the author's own v2 concedes; the v2 bound is the only claim now standing.

withdrawn.what: The v1 claim that mu = 0 for almost all good ordinary primes was replaced in v2 by the weaker bound mu <= 1 for all but finitely many primes.

events.direction: Partial and weaker than the elliptic-curve conjecture. Not about the number-field statement.

events.what_happened: Peikai Qi and Matt Stokes, arXiv:2408.03836, 'On the Non p-Rationality and Iwasawa Invariants of Certain Real Quadratic Fields' (7 Aug 2024). Real quadratic fields K = Q(sqrt(m^2 p^(2r) + 1)); shows non-p-rationality for an infinite family; for m = 1 and non-Wieferich p, the abstract says 'then the Iwasawa invariants for cyclotomic Z_p-extension of K vanish', which the fetch summary reads as conditional on p not dividing the class number of K.
events.delivers: For the stated family of real quadratic fields (m = 1, non-Wieferich p, and the m-bound), vanishing of the cyclotomic Iwasawa invariants of K, on the hypothesis (as summarised from the abstract, not confirmed in full text) that p does not divide the class number of K. Covers one family of real quadratic fields at a prime p depending on the family.
events.remains: All other real quadratic fields, all other totally real fields, and the statement for all primes p.
events.doubts: The exact hypothesis is taken from a fetch summary of the abstract; the full text was not read.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for a family; conditional by the reading above.

events.what_happened: Mohamed Mahmoud Chems-Eddin, arXiv:2409.13574, 'On the maximal unramified pro-2-extension of Z_2-extension of certain real biquadratic fields' (v1 20 Sep 2024; v2 25 Jul 2026). Constructs families of real biquadratic fields of degree 2^(n+2) whose 2-class group is Z/2 x Z/2 and whose cyclotomic Z_2-layers have unramified abelian 2-Iwasawa module Z/2 x Z/2; the abstract says 'hence these fields satisfy Greenberg's conjecture'.
events.revisions: v1 20 Sep 2024; v2 25 Jul 2026 (I did not compare the versions).
events.delivers: For the constructed families of real biquadratic fields, at p = 2, the author states that Greenberg's conjecture holds, via a computed Iwasawa module. Families only.
events.remains: All other real biquadratic fields, all totally real fields, and all odd primes p.
events.doubts: The v2 date (25 Jul 2026) is about 22 months after v1; whether the family or the claim changed is unknown because I read only the abstract.
events.direction: In favour of the conjecture for the families stated; family-restricted.

events.what_happened: Peikai Qi and Matt Stokes, arXiv:2410.05706, 'An Analogue of Greenberg's Conjecture for CM Fields' (8 Oct 2024). For a CM field K with totally real K+, split primes and a chosen set S of half the primes above p, under Leopoldt's conjecture: criteria for mu = lambda = 0 of the S-ramified Z_p-extension; a numerical criterion for imaginary biquadratic fields analogous to Fukuda-Komatsu.
events.delivers: Criteria for mu = lambda = 0 for the S-ramified Z_p-extension of CM fields (under split and Leopoldt hypotheses) and a numerical criterion for imaginary biquadratic fields. This is an analogue on a different extension of a different class of fields.
events.remains: The conjecture as stated: totally real fields and the cyclotomic Z_p-extension.
events.direction: Neutral to the bullet; an analogue, which the abstract itself calls analogous.

events.what_happened: Pietro Mercuri, Maurizio Paoluzi and Rene Schoof, arXiv:2503.00819, 'Greenberg's conjecture for real quadratic number fields' (2 Mar 2025). Computes the 3-class groups of the layers of the cyclotomic Z_3-extensions of 30,394 real quadratic fields Q(sqrt(f)) with discriminant f < 100,000. Theorem 1.1 as read: 'Greenberg's conjecture is true for p = 3 and the real quadratic fields of discriminant f < 100,000.' Published as J. Exp. Math. 1(2) 207-217 (2025), DOI 10.56994/JXM.001.002.001 (journal listing from a search result, not opened).
events.revisions: v1 only, 2 Mar 2025 (per arXiv listing); journal version in J. Exp. Math. 2025.
events.delivers: For p = 3 and the 30,394 listed real quadratic fields: the orders of A_n stay bounded, so lambda_3 = 0 for those fields (mu vanishes for abelian fields by Ferrero-Washington). A finite computation; no general argument.
events.remains: The conjecture for every other prime p, every real quadratic field of discriminant at least 100,000, all real fields of higher degree, and the generalized conjecture.

checked_by.who: Journal of Experimental Mathematics (editorial and refereeing process)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the article in vol. 1, issue 2 (2025)

events.directly_checkable: The 30,394 fields and their class groups are checkable by a computer algebra system; the html version names Magma and PARI/GP (refs [1], [14]). I did not check the code or data.
events.direction: In favour of the conjecture for the finitely many fields listed (instances, not a move in the universal claim).

events.what_happened: Mohamed Mahmoud Chems-Eddin, arXiv:2503.15727, 'Greenberg's conjecture and Iwasawa module of Real biquadratic fields I' (19 Mar 2025; v2 14 Oct 2025). Gives several families of real biquadratic fields for which the 2-Iwasawa module is trivial, cyclic of order 2^n, or Z/2 x Z/2^n; poses the problem of which such fields have equal 2-rank of the Iwasawa module and of the first-layer class group. Published in J. Number Theory 281 (2026) 224-266 (per the arXiv journal reference).
events.revisions: v1 19 Mar 2025; v2 14 Oct 2025 (42 pages, to appear in J. Number Theory).
events.delivers: For the listed families of real biquadratic fields: a finite (trivial or cyclic or Z/2 x Z/2^n) 2-Iwasawa module, which gives lambda_2 = mu_2 = 0 for those fields. Families only; p = 2.
events.remains: All other real biquadratic fields, all other degrees, all odd primes, and the conjecture as a whole.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published in vol. 281 (2026), pp. 224-266, per the arXiv journal reference

events.direction: In favour of the conjecture for the families stated; family-restricted.

events.what_happened: Thong Nguyen Quang Do, arXiv:2505.07529, 'On Greenberg's generalized conjecture for families of number fields' (12 May 2025). For imaginary k, the generalized conjecture (X~(k~) pseudo-null) is implied by pseudo-nullity conditions on a special Z_p^2-extension of k; the author shows these conditions hold fully or partly for certain families of number fields. The abstract says very few theoretical results toward the generalized conjecture are known.
events.revisions: v1 only, 12 May 2025 (the HTML render is dated October 2025, which I take to be a later compilation of v1).
events.delivers: A reduction of the generalized (pseudo-null) conjecture for imaginary k to pseudo-nullity conditions on a Z_p^2-extension, shown to hold fully or partly for some families. Whether any family is then settled unconditionally is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: The generalized conjecture for real fields and for general number fields, and the unconditional statement for all imaginary fields.
events.doubts: The reduction is conditional on pseudo-nullity conditions which the abstract says hold only partly or for families.
events.direction: Partial reduction; neither proves nor refutes the generalized conjecture.

events.what_happened: Mohamed Mahmoud Chems-Eddin and Hamza El Mamry, arXiv:2601.07067, 'Greenberg's conjecture and Iwasawa module of Real biquadratic fields II' (11 Jan 2026). Gives families of real biquadratic fields where the 2-rank of the class group is stable in the cyclotomic Z_2-extension; the abstract says 'Greenberg's conjecture is verified for some new families of number fields'; determines the complete list of real biquadratic fields with trivial 2-Iwasawa module (Theorem 4.2 per the html).
events.delivers: Greenberg's conjecture (p = 2) verified for the stated families of real biquadratic fields; the complete list of real biquadratic fields with trivial 2-Iwasawa module, which gives lambda = mu = 0 for those fields. Family-restricted; biquadratic only.
events.remains: Totally real fields that are not biquadratic, all odd primes, and the conjecture as a whole.
events.direction: In favour of the conjecture for the families stated; family-restricted.

events.what_happened: Qinhao Li and Derong Qiu, arXiv:2603.05142, 'Iwasawa invariants and class number parity of multi-quadratic number fields' (5 Mar 2026; v2 16 Jun 2026). Explicit results for lambda_2 of cyclotomic Z_2-extensions via Hasse's unit index and ramification; for imaginary multi-quadratic fields an explicit lambda_2 formula is obtained assuming Greenberg's conjecture; applied to class number parity.
events.delivers: Conditional: an explicit formula for lambda_2 of imaginary multi-quadratic fields under Greenberg's conjecture. Unconditional explicit results for lambda_2 of some fields (not specified in the abstract). Does not prove the conjecture.
events.remains: The conjecture itself, for all totally real fields and all primes.
events.doubts: The arXiv page lists 'Journal of Number Theory, 291 (2027), 304-327'. That volume postdates today (11 Oct 2026), so the journal reference cannot be verified and I do not treat the paper as accepted.
events.direction: Uses the conjecture as a hypothesis; does not move it.

events.what_happened: Josue Avila and Foivos Chnaras, arXiv:2605.09111, 'On the Iwasawa lambda-invariant of the cyclotomic Z_2-extension of a family of real quadratic fields in which 2 splits' (9 May 2026). For K = Q(sqrt(pq)) under congruence conditions on p and q, a Legendre-symbol condition and power-residue conditions, proves lambda_2(K) = 0. Method: Greenberg's criterion for the split prime case plus a capitulation argument modelled on Kumakawa; key new input is a square-class computation of the Hasse unit index giving q(K_2) <= 2. The conditions as given in a search summary: p = 1 mod 8, q = 9 mod 16, (p/q) = -1 (not checked against the text).
events.delivers: lambda_2(K) = 0 for a family of real quadratic fields Q(sqrt(pq)) under the stated congruence and symbol conditions. Family-restricted; p = 2.
events.remains: All other real quadratic fields, all other totally real fields, and all odd primes.
events.direction: In favour of the conjecture for the stated family.

events.what_happened: Anwesh Ray, arXiv:2607.10728, 'Greenberg's mu = 0 conjecture for lisse sheaves over global function fields' (v1 12 Jul 2026; v2 14 Jul 2026). Over a global function field K of characteristic p and a Z_l-extension (l != p), proves the Pontryagin dual of Selmer groups of lisse Z_l-sheaves has mu-invariant zero; the author calls this a positive-characteristic, prime-to-p analogue of Greenberg's mu = 0 conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 12 Jul 2026; v2 14 Jul 2026 (22 pages, added a section on Greenberg Selmer groups).
events.delivers: An analogue over global function fields for Selmer groups of lisse sheaves. Does not concern number fields.
events.remains: The number-field conjecture entirely.
events.direction: Analogue; neutral to the number-field statement.

events.what_happened: Chen Lin and Xuejun Guo, arXiv:2607.21250, 'The p-rationality of Q(sqrt(-(kp+m))) and Q(sqrt(p(p+1)))' (v1 23 Jul 2026; v2 31 Aug 2026). Constructs imaginary and real quadratic fields that are p-rational: the imaginary family for sufficiently large p (via Louboutin's class number bound), and Q(sqrt(p(p+1))) for all odd primes p, plus new triquadratic examples. The abstract does not mention Greenberg's p-rationality conjecture.
events.delivers: For the case t = 1 of the rationality conjecture (a p-rational quadratic field with Galois group Z/2), the abstract's real family Q(sqrt(p(p+1))) would supply one for each odd p, if its claim holds as stated. The abstract does not frame this as the conjecture. Earlier results (Benmerieme-Movahhedi, date not established) already give infinitely many real quadratic p-rational fields for each odd p, per a search summary. Nothing for t >= 2.
events.remains: The conjecture for every t >= 2, and the general (Z/2Z)^t statement.
events.direction: Neutral to the conjecture except as a t = 1 instance; the authors do not link it to Greenberg.

events.what_happened: Zichao Lin and Mulun Yin, arXiv:2609.40282, 'On Greenberg's conjecture for rational elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes' (30 Sep 2026, single version). For an elliptic curve E/Q, an odd good ordinary prime p, and a rational p-isogeny (Eisenstein case): proves Greenberg's conjecture that the algebraic mu-invariant of the Selmer group over Q_p^cyc vanishes. Theorem A as read: 'Let E/Q be an elliptic curve, and let p be an odd good ordinary Eisenstein prime for E. Then Greenberg's conjecture holds.' Also: 'When E has multiplicative reduction at p, the algebraic part of Greenberg's conjecture holds.' Uses the Iwasawa Main Conjecture at Eisenstein primes (cited as Castella-Grossi-Skinner, Greenberg-Vatsal and Keller-Yin) to confirm Stevens's analytic mu-behaviour. The paper says its case (ii) (phi unramified and even, psi ramified and odd) is the one Greenberg-Vatsal did not treat, and that Trifkovic's method differs. The Wikipedia lead cites this paper (as arXiv 2609.40282v1) for the claim that 'Greenberg's invariants conjecture appears to have been resolved as of 2026'.
events.delivers: For elliptic curves E/Q with an odd good ordinary Eisenstein prime p (equivalently a rational p-isogeny): the algebraic mu-invariant of the Selmer group over Q_p^cyc vanishes, which the paper calls the algebraic part of Greenberg's elliptic-curve conjecture; also Stevens's analytic mu-behaviour, via the Main Conjecture. The text read does not address lambda or mu of totally real number fields; no step from the Selmer mu-invariant of elliptic curves to the invariants of totally real fields appears in the parts I read.
events.remains: The number-field invariants conjecture (lambda = mu = 0 for totally real k) entirely; the elliptic-curve conjecture for primes p with E[p] irreducible (the main case of Greenberg's elliptic conjecture, not Eisenstein).
events.doubts: Single version posted 11 days before this record; no referee, expert write-up, citation or review found in searches. Its case (ii) is the step earlier work left open, so a check would look there. The arXiv listing shows no affiliations and I did not establish the qualifications of Zichao Lin; Mulun Yin is cited as co-author of Keller-Yin (arXiv:2402.12781), a paper the text cites as part of the Main Conjecture input. The paper's Main Conjecture input rests on Castella-Grossi-Skinner (Math. Ann. 2025) and Keller-Yin.
events.direction: If correct, a proof of the elliptic-curve Selmer mu-part for Eisenstein primes; does not bear on the number-field statement except through the Wikipedia citation, which treats it as the invariants conjecture.
people: Francesc Castella (thanked in acknowledgements for pointing out Trifkovic and Stevens)

events.what_happened: Ralph Greenberg, 1976 paper on p-adic L-functions and cyclotomic fields: necessary and sufficient conditions for lambda = mu = 0 in two opposite cases (p inert in F; p splitting completely in F), per a search summary of that paper. The 1971 thesis is the origin of the conjecture.
events.delivers: Criteria equivalent to lambda = mu = 0 in the inert and totally split prime cases. Partial criteria, not a proof of the conjecture.
events.remains: The conjecture for all primes and totally real fields.
events.direction: Partial criteria; neutral.

events.what_happened: Ferrero and Washington proved that mu_l(k) = 0 for the cyclotomic Z_l-extension of every abelian number field k over Q (the article states this; year and primary text not retrieved).
events.delivers: mu = 0 for all abelian number fields over Q, so the mu-part of the invariants conjecture for those fields; lambda is not covered.
events.remains: lambda = 0 for totally real fields, mu for non-abelian fields, and the general mu conjecture (part c).
events.direction: In favour of the mu-part for abelian fields.

events.what_happened: Ichimura and Sumida, J. Math. Sci. Univ. Tokyo (1996) and Tohoku Math. J. (1997): a criterion for the conjecture via cyclotomic units and p-adic L-functions, used to show lambda_3(Q(sqrt(m))) = 0 for all m < 10^4 (as summarised in the Mercuri et al. paper's introduction and a search summary; not opened).
events.delivers: lambda_3 = 0 for real quadratic fields Q(sqrt(m)), m < 10^4, under the criterion's hypotheses. Family-restricted, p = 3.
events.remains: All other real quadratic fields and all other primes.
events.doubts: Taken from a search summary, not the paper.
events.direction: In favour, family-restricted.

events.what_happened: Mizusawa (2000): lambda_3 = 0 for Q(sqrt(39345017)), using the Ichimura-Sumida criterion and the infinite 3-class field tower of that field (as cited in the Mercuri et al. introduction; not opened).
events.delivers: lambda_3 = 0 for one real quadratic field.
events.remains: Every other field.
events.direction: In favour, single field.

events.what_happened: William McCallum, arXiv:math/0007209 (July 2000), 'Greenberg's conjecture and units in multiple Z_p-extensions': proves the generalized (pseudo-null) conjecture for K = Q(mu_p) when p has irregularity index 1, Vandiver's conjecture holds, and a mild unit hypothesis is satisfied (as summarised in a search result; not opened).
events.delivers: The generalized conjecture for one class of cyclotomic fields under extra hypotheses (irregularity index 1, Vandiver, unit condition).
events.remains: The generalized conjecture for other fields and for totally real fields generally.
events.direction: In favour, conditional on extra hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Razvan Barbulescu and Jishnu Ray, arXiv:1706.04847 (June 2017), 'Numerical verification of the Cohen-Lenstra-Martinet heuristics and of Greenberg's p-rationality conjecture'; Journal de Theorie des Nombres de Bordeaux 32 (2020) 159-177. Numerical experiments supporting Greenberg's p-rationality conjecture; a family of p-rational biquadratic fields; and, per a search summary, GC((Z/2Z)^t, p) for primes 5 <= p <= 97 and some range of t. The heuristic argument for multiquadratic and multicubic fields is tied to Cohen-Lenstra-Martinet and a conjecture of Hofmann and Zhang.
events.revisions: arXiv v3 on the abstract page; JTNB 2020 published version.
events.delivers: Numerical verification of the rationality conjecture for particular primes and t, and a family of p-rational biquadratic fields. Family- and range-restricted; the search summary's range for t was not checked against the text.
events.remains: The rationality conjecture for all odd primes and all t.

checked_by.who: Journal de Theorie des Nombres de Bordeaux (referee process)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published as JTNB 32 (2020), no. 1, 159-177 (per a search result; not opened)

events.directly_checkable: p-rationality checks by a PARI/GP program, per the authors' companion page as summarised.
events.direction: Numerical support; not a proof.

disputes.summary: Wikipedia's 'Greenberg's conjectures' lead (retrieved 7-11 October 2026) says the general conjecture 'was unsolved as of 2025' (citing Do, arXiv:2505.07529) and that 'Greenberg's invariants conjecture appears to have been resolved as of 2026', citing arXiv:2609.40282 (Lin-Yin). The cited paper's Theorem A is about the Selmer mu-invariant of elliptic curves E/Q at odd good ordinary Eisenstein primes; the article body has no elliptic-curve section, and the cited paper does not mention totally real number fields or lambda. The article's own reference title is 'On Greenberg's conjecture for rational elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes'. Read as stated, the citation supports a different conjecture from the one the sentence names. The article also carries a 'has multiple issues' banner.

Search summaries and a Wikipedia search snippet give 'unsolved as of 2012' (Greenberg's 1971 thesis conjecture) and an older version of the article that described both conjectures as unsolved as of 2021. These are older statuses, superseded by the 2025 and 2026 sentences; I did not open the older revisions.
arXiv:2603.05142 lists 'Journal of Number Theory, 291 (2027), 304-327', a volume dated after the date of this record. The journal reference cannot be verified.

summary: Greenberg's conjectures, as the current Wikipedia article gives them, are four things: the invariants conjecture (lambda = mu = 0 for totally real k and all p), the generalized pseudo-null conjecture (2001), a further mu_l(k) = 0 claim for all number fields, and the 2016 rationality conjecture on (Z/2Z)^t p-rational fields. I searched 42 times (listed verbatim below) and opened the Wikipedia article, the arXiv abstracts or html of about 20 papers, the openai/math README and an OpenAI-results index. Across 2024-2026 I found no proof of the invariants conjecture or the generalized conjecture. The results in the window are: a finite computation for p = 3 and 30,394 real quadratic fields (Mercuri-Paoluzi-Schoof, 2025, J. Exp. Math.); family-restricted verifications for real biquadratic fields at p = 2 (Chems-Eddin 2024, 2025, 2026; Chems-Eddin and El Mamry 2026, with a complete list of real biquadratic fields with trivial 2-Iwasawa module); a family of real quadratic fields with lambda_2 = 0 (Avila-Chnaras, May 2026); a conditional reduction of the generalized conjecture for imaginary fields (Do, 2025); and conditional explicit formulas assuming the conjecture (Li-Qiu, 2026). Two in-window elliptic-curve items are not about the number-field statement: Chakravarthy (2024), who withdrew a v1 claim of mu = 0 for almost all primes in v2 and now claims only mu <= 1 for all but finitely many primes; and Lin-Yin (30 September 2026), which claims the elliptic-curve Selmer mu = 0 for odd good ordinary Eisenstein primes, including case (ii) that Greenberg-Vatsal did not treat. Lin-Yin is the source of the Wikipedia lead's claim that the invariants conjecture was 'resolved as of 2026'. The cited paper concerns a different conjecture, so I record that claim as a scope mismatch rather than a resolution. Close calls: (1) Lin-Yin. It is a substantial claim about a conjecture carrying Greenberg's name, its scope is elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes, and it is only 11 days old with no uptake found; the Wikipedia citation is the only route by which it reaches the bullet. (2) The family results (Mercuri et al.; Chems-Eddin I and II; Avila-Chnaras; Qi-Stokes 2024). Each verifies lambda or the Iwasawa module for specific fields. They are instances of a universal claim, not a change in a quantity the statement names, so I record them as instances, with the reading that they move a count of verified fields and no quantity in the bullet. (3) The Lin-Guo 2026 quadratic result is a t = 1 instance of the rationality conjecture, if its real family Q(sqrt(p(p+1))) is p-rational for all odd p as the abstract says; the authors do not connect it to Greenberg, and earlier quadratic results may already cover t = 1. AI: no source in the window or before, read for this record, names an AI system in connection with this problem. I checked the OpenAI Astra list of ten results (1 August 2026; from coverage, primary post not opened): none concerns Iwasawa theory or Greenberg's conjectures. I checked the openai/math release (README: 719 manuscripts in 372 result families, dated only by a 2026 footer): no Iwasawa or Greenberg term appears in the visible text. The full catalogue and its 31 number-theory families were not enumerated. The Count Ex Machina / 'GPT, the Counterexample Machine' paper (arXiv:2608.29595, Sra) does not mention Greenberg or Iwasawa invariants. The AI checks rest on abstracts and visible text; full texts of several papers were not readable (see incomplete). Where a source has been read only in abstract, none_found true means no system is named in what I read, not that the full text was checked.
competing_reading: Read the Wikipedia lead's 2026 sentence and the Lin-Yin paper together. The article's editor treats Lin-Yin as resolving the invariants conjecture, and the paper calls its result 'Greenberg's conjecture'. If the proof holds and the same name is taken to pick out the same problem, the bullet becomes resolved on 30 September 2026, after the frozen window, and the judging pass would count a resolution. Against this: the paper's Theorem A concerns the Selmer mu-invariant of elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes, the text I read never mentions totally real fields or lambda, and the article body has no elliptic-curve section. A reader who counts it as the invariants conjecture would be reading the name, not the quantity. For the families: one can say each verified family moves the set of totally real fields where the conjecture is known, and that the bullet asks about every such field. Against that, a verified field is a finite instance of a universal claim, the same logic the DEEP_DIVE gives for Collatz-type cases, so the count is of instances and nothing in the bullet's quantities moves.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The Wikipedia article's edit history and its reference [2]: who added the 2026 sentence, when, and what the reference supports. (2) A human reading of Lin-Yin's Theorem A for case (ii), together with a check of whether any step applies to lambda or mu of a totally real field; I expect none, and an expert write-up or a citing paper would confirm it. (3) The frozen January 2024 wording of the bullet, to establish whether the elliptic-curve and rationality conjectures were in scope. (4) The full openai/math catalogue (719 manuscripts, 372 families) searched for Iwasawa and Greenberg terms, and OpenAI's primary Astra post for its ten results. (5) A search of arXiv math.NT listings from 2024 to 2026 for 'Greenberg' in titles and abstracts, to catch any family or general result I did not see.

event.what_happened: Peikai Qi and Matt Stokes, arXiv:2408.03836, 'On the Non p-Rationality and Iwasawa Invariants of Certain Real Quadratic Fields' (7 Aug 2024). Real quadratic fields K = Q(sqrt(m^2 p^(2r) + 1)); shows non-p-rationality for an infinite family; for m = 1 and non-Wieferich p, the abstract says 'then the Iwasawa invariants for cyclotomic Z_p-extension of K vanish', which the fetch summary reads as conditional on p not dividing the class number of K.
event.delivers: For the stated family of real quadratic fields (m = 1, non-Wieferich p, and the m-bound), vanishing of the cyclotomic Iwasawa invariants of K, on the hypothesis (as summarised from the abstract, not confirmed in full text) that p does not divide the class number of K. Covers one family of real quadratic fields at a prime p depending on the family.
event.remains: All other real quadratic fields, all other totally real fields, and the statement for all primes p.
event.doubts: The exact hypothesis is taken from a fetch summary of the abstract; the full text was not read.
event.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for a family; conditional by the reading above.

events.credibility_reason: The v1 claim (mu = 0 for almost all primes) was conceded wrong by the author after Lei and Gajek-Leonard found an error; only the weaker v2 bound stands.

judgement.why: The statement names Greenberg's conjectures on number fields: the invariants conjecture for totally real fields, plus the generalized pseudo-null conjecture and related claims. Results proving lambda = mu = 0 for infinite families of totally real fields (Qi-Stokes real quadratic, Chems-Eddin's biquadratic families, Chems-Eddin-El Mamry, Avila-Chnaras) restrict the universal statement to a class of fields, so they are cases rather than finite instances. Mercuri-Paoluzi-Schoof covers 30,394 explicitly listed fields, which is a finite check, so it is instances. Ichimura-Sumida, Mizusawa and the Barbulescu-Ray numerics are instances for the same reason. The elliptic-curve mu conjecture shares Greenberg's name but is a different conjecture, so I scored Chakravarthy and Lin-Yin as variant. This includes Lin-Yin, which Wikipedia's 2026 lead cites as resolving the invariants conjecture: the record shows the paper never addresses totally real fields or lambda, so the citation is a scope error. The CM-field and function-field analogues are variants too. Do, Li-Qiu and McCallum are reductions, or are conditional on unproven hypotheses (Vandiver's conjecture, pseudo-nullity conditions), so they are none. Lin-Guo gives at most t = 1 of the rationality conjecture, and the record says earlier results already supply that, so it is none. Chems-Eddin I is accepted in J. Number Theory, so it counts as digested. No AI system is credited anywhere.
judgement.doubts: The frozen January 2024 wording was not retrieved, so it is unclear whether the elliptic-curve and rationality conjectures were inside the bullet; if the elliptic-curve conjecture were in scope, Lin-Yin would be a case (Eisenstein primes), not a variant. Qi-Stokes 2024's hypothesis comes from an abstract summary. Whether Chems-Eddin 2409.13574's families are infinite was read only from the abstract. The AI search of the openai/math catalogue was partial.
